     3	/-!
     4	# Finite controlled unitaries
     5	
     6	A complete projective measurement controls a family of operators on a second
     7	finite-dimensional space. Orthogonality of the measurement effects makes
     8	multiplication of the resulting operator sums componentwise. In particular,
     9	unitary components give a unitary controlled operator.
    10	
    11	These are formalization-only algebraic lemmas, not the extraction theorem:
    12	they do not construct the global measurement or establish the Pauli relations.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1700`,
    17	  the unitarity calculation in the proof of `lem:qld-unitary`.
    18	- Blueprint `def:v-swap-unitary` and `lem:v-swap-conjugation`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	variable {Outcome Control Target : Type*}
    28	variable [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype Control] [DecidableEq Control]
    29	variable [Fintype Target]
    30	
    31	/-- Multiplication of operator sums controlled by the same projective measurement
    32	is componentwise. This isolates the orthogonality calculation in the proof of
    33	`lem:qld-unitary`, before any unitarity of the controlled components is used. -/
    34	theorem sum_heteroKron_mul_sum_heteroKron
    35	    (measurement : Measurement Outcome Control)
    36	    (hprojective : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective measurement)
    37	    (leftOperators rightOperators : Outcome → Op Target) :
    38	    (∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome) (leftOperators outcome)) *
    39	        (∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome) (rightOperators outcome)) =
    40	      ∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome)
    41	        (leftOperators outcome * rightOperators outcome) := by
    42	  classical
    43	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    44	  simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum, heteroKron_mul]
    45	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    46	  intro outcome _
    47	  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single outcome]
    48	  · rw [(hprojective outcome).isIdempotentElem.eq]
    49	  · intro other _ hother
    50	    rw [DistanceCalculus.projective_effect_mul_effect_eq_zero
    51	      measurement hprojective hother.symm]
    52	    exact Matrix.zero_kronecker _
    53	  · simp
    54	
    55	variable [DecidableEq Target]
    56	
    57	/-- A controlled operator times its adjoint is the identity when each component
    58	times its adjoint is the identity. This is the finite controlled-unitary
    59	calculation at paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1700`,
    60	with arbitrary unitary components in place of the products of Pauli observables. -/
    61	theorem sum_heteroKron_mul_conjTranspose
    62	    (measurement : Measurement Outcome Control)
    63	    (hprojective : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective measurement)
    64	    (operators : Outcome → Op Target)
    65	    (hunitary : ∀ outcome, operators outcome * (operators outcome)ᴴ = 1) :
    66	    (∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome) (operators outcome)) *
    67	        (∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome) (operators outcome))ᴴ = 1 := by
    68	  have hself (outcome : Outcome) :
    69	      (measurement.effect outcome)ᴴ = measurement.effect outcome :=
    70	    (hprojective outcome).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
    71	  calc
    72	    _ = (∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome) (operators outcome)) *
    73	        (∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome) ((operators outcome)ᴴ)) := by
    74	      simp only [Matrix.conjTranspose_sum, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
    75	        Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker, hself]
    76	    _ = ∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome)
    77	        (operators outcome * (operators outcome)ᴴ) :=
    78	      sum_heteroKron_mul_sum_heteroKron measurement hprojective _ _
    79	    _ = ∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome) (1 : Op Target) := by
    80	      simp_rw [hunitary]
    81	    _ = 1 := by
    82	      rw [← DistanceCalculus.heteroKron_finset_sum_left, measurement.sum_eq_one,
    83	        heteroKron_one_one]
    84	
    85	/-- The reverse adjoint product of a controlled operator is also the identity.
    86	For finite square matrices, Mathlib's `mul_eq_one_comm` converts either inverse
    87	identity to the other, both for the components and for the controlled operator.
    88	This supplies the reverse identity implicit in the same source calculation. -/
    89	theorem conjTranspose_mul_sum_heteroKron
    90	    (measurement : Measurement Outcome Control)
    91	    (hprojective : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective measurement)
    92	    (operators : Outcome → Op Target)
    93	    (hunitary : ∀ outcome, (operators outcome)ᴴ * operators outcome = 1) :
    94	    (∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome) (operators outcome))ᴴ *
    95	        (∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome) (operators outcome)) = 1 := by
    96	  apply mul_eq_one_comm.mp
    97	  apply sum_heteroKron_mul_conjTranspose measurement hprojective operators
    98	  intro outcome
    99	  exact mul_eq_one_comm.mp (hunitary outcome)
   100	
   101	/-- A finite sum of unitary operators controlled by a complete projective
   102	measurement is unitary. The hypotheses concern the actual component operators;
   103	no unitarity or extraction conclusion is assumed for their controlled sum. -/
   104	theorem sum_heteroKron_mem_unitary
   105	    (measurement : Measurement Outcome Control)
   106	    (hprojective : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective measurement)
   107	    (operators : Outcome → Op Target)
   108	    (hunitary : ∀ outcome, operators outcome ∈ unitary (Op Target)) :
   109	    (∑ outcome, heteroKron (measurement.effect outcome) (operators outcome)) ∈
   110	      unitary (Op (Control × Target)) := by
   111	  exact ⟨conjTranspose_mul_sum_heteroKron measurement hprojective operators
   112	      (fun outcome => (hunitary outcome).1),
   113	    sum_heteroKron_mul_conjTranspose measurement hprojective operators
   114	      (fun outcome => (hunitary outcome).2)⟩
   115	
   116	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

     4	/-!

    21	/-- Multiplying a normalized restricted average by its retained mass gives the
    22	unnormalized restricted sum. This formalization-only identity supports
    23	proof-only conditioning in `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper
    24	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`; it changes no game distribution. -/
    25	theorem avgOver_restrict_mul_mass {Sample : Type*} [DecidableEq Sample]
    26	    (dist : Distribution Sample) (good : Sample -> Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    27	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample)
    28	    (value : Sample -> ℝ) :
    29	    (∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample) *
    30	      avgOver (Distribution.restrict dist good hpos) value =
    31	      ∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample * value sample := by
    32	  unfold avgOver Distribution.restrict
    33	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    34	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    35	  intro sample hsample
    36	  simp only [if_pos (Finset.mem_filter.mp hsample).2]
    37	  field_simp
    38	
    39	/-- Conditioning a nonnegative finite average inflates its bound by at most
    40	the inverse retained mass. This is a formalization-only finite probability
    41	estimate used in the conditioning step of `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper
    42	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`. -/
    43	theorem avgOver_restrict_le_div_mass {Sample : Type*} [DecidableEq Sample]
    44	    (dist : Distribution Sample) (good : Sample -> Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    45	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample)
    46	    (value : Sample -> ℝ) (hnonneg : ∀ sample, 0 ≤ value sample) :
    47	    avgOver (Distribution.restrict dist good hpos) value ≤
    48	      avgOver dist value /
    49	        (∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample) := by
    50	  apply (le_div_iff₀ hpos).mpr
    51	  rw [mul_comm, avgOver_restrict_mul_mass]
    52	  exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.filter_subset _ _)
    53	    (fun sample _ _ => mul_nonneg (dist.nonnegative sample) (hnonneg sample))
    54	
    55	/-- An average of a function bounded above by one is at most the retained mass
    56	times its conditional average, plus the discarded probability mass. This
    57	formalization-only estimate restores the original distribution after proof-only
    58	conditioning in `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper
    59	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`. No discarded mass is omitted. -/
    60	theorem avgOver_le_restrict_add_discarded_mass {Sample : Type*} [DecidableEq Sample]
    61	    (dist : Distribution Sample) (good : Sample -> Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    62	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample)
    63	    (value : Sample -> ℝ) (hunit : ∀ sample, value sample ≤ 1) :
    64	    avgOver dist value ≤
    65	      (∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample) *
    66	        avgOver (Distribution.restrict dist good hpos) value +
    67	      ∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter (fun sample => ¬ good sample), dist.weight sample := by
    68	  classical
    69	  rw [avgOver_restrict_mul_mass]
    70	  unfold avgOver
    71	  rw [← Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not dist.support good
    72	    (fun sample => dist.weight sample * value sample)]
    73	  exact add_le_add_right (Finset.sum_le_sum fun sample _ =>
    74	    mul_le_of_le_one_right (dist.nonnegative sample) (hunit sample)) _
    75	
    76	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Completion on a prescribed set of outcomes
     5	
     6	This formalization-only auxiliary constructs a complete measurement supported on
     7	the good outcomes of a finite measurement, by sending every bad outcome to a
     8	specified good outcome. For projective measurements this adds the complementary
     9	projection to the default effect and preserves projectivity. The consistency
    10	estimates charge changes of outcome labels only to the state mass of that
    11	complementary projection, on either of two possibly different player spaces.
    12	
    13	The source-specific estimate on the mass outside the image of the polynomial
    14	combining map is the unimplemented target `global_polynomial_bad_mass_le`,
    15	specified in `audits/2026-09-06_supported-projective-completion.md` under issue #279.
    16	No result here asserts the global polynomial-pair theorem or derives that estimate.
    17	
    18	## References
    19	
    20	* `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1364-1402`,
    21	  the completion step after `eq:qld-sgg-mhat-sandwich` in `lem:qld-4-7`.
    22	* Blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`, whose source theorem remains separate from this auxiliary.
    23	-/

    33	variable {α β X ι ιA ιB : Type*}
    34	variable [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    35	variable [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]

    37	variable [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]

    39	/-- Retain every good outcome and send every other outcome to the specified
    40	good outcome. The default is actual domain data, with its membership proof. -/
    41	def toGood (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    42	    (a₀ : {a // good a}) (a : α) : {a // good a} :=
    43	  if h : good a then ⟨a, h⟩ else a₀
    44	
    45	omit [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] in
    46	@[simp] theorem toGood_coe (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    47	    (a₀ a : {a // good a}) : toGood good a₀ a = a := by
    48	  simp [toGood, a.property]
    49	
    50	/-- The omitted effects. When the measurement is projective, their sum is the
    51	projection complementary to the sum of good effects. -/
    52	noncomputable def badEffect (M : Measurement α ι)
    53	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] : Op ι :=
    54	  ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => ¬ good a), M.effect a
    55	
    56	/-- Complete the restriction to good outcomes by adding all bad effects to
    57	`a₀`. This is an outcome postprocessing of the original complete measurement. -/
    58	noncomputable def complete (M : Measurement α ι)
    59	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (a₀ : {a // good a}) :
    60	    Measurement {a // good a} ι :=
    61	  M.postprocess (toGood good a₀)
    62	
    63	/-- The completion is projective whenever the original measurement is
    64	projective, by projectivity of outcome postprocessing. -/
    65	theorem complete_isProjective (M : Measurement α ι)
    66	    (hM : Measurement.IsProjective M) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    67	    (a₀ : {a // good a}) : Measurement.IsProjective (complete M good a₀) :=
    68	  SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective M hM (toGood good a₀)
    69	
    70	omit [DecidableEq α] in
    71	/-- The bad effect is precisely the complement of the restricted total. -/
    72	theorem badEffect_eq_one_sub (M : Measurement α ι)
    73	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] :
    74	    badEffect M good = 1 - ∑ a : {a // good a}, M.effect a := by
    75	  have hsplit := Fintype.sum_subtype_add_sum_subtype good M.effect
    76	  have hbad : badEffect M good = ∑ a : {a // ¬ good a}, M.effect a := by
    77	    exact Finset.sum_subtype _ (by simp) M.effect
    78	  rw [hbad]
    79	  rw [M.sum_eq_one] at hsplit
    80	  exact eq_sub_of_add_eq' hsplit
    81	
    82	omit [DecidableEq α] in
    83	/-- The sum of the omitted effects is positive semidefinite. -/
    84	theorem badEffect_nonneg (M : Measurement α ι)
    85	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] : 0 ≤ badEffect M good :=
    86	  Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    87	
    88	/-- The submeasurement obtained by retaining only the good outcomes. -/
    89	noncomputable def restrict (M : Measurement α ι)
    90	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] : Submeasurement {a // good a} ι where
    91	  effect a := M.effect a
    92	  pos a := M.pos a
    93	  sum_le_one := by
    94	    have h := badEffect_nonneg M good
    95	    rw [badEffect_eq_one_sub] at h
    96	    exact sub_nonneg.mp h

    98	/-- The bad effect is itself a projection: it is one effect of the binary
    99	postprocessing recording whether an outcome is bad. -/
   100	theorem badEffect_isStarProjection (M : Measurement α ι)
   101	    (hM : Measurement.IsProjective M) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] :
   102	    IsStarProjection (badEffect M good) := by
   103	  have h := SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective M hM
   104	    (fun a => decide (¬ good a)) true
   105	  change IsStarProjection (∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter
   106	    (fun a => decide (¬ good a) = true), M.effect a) at h
   107	  simpa only [decide_eq_true_eq, badEffect] using h
   108	
   109	/-- The completed default effect absorbs exactly the omitted projection;
   110	all other good effects are retained. -/
   111	theorem complete_effect (M : Measurement α ι)
   112	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (a₀ a : {a // good a}) :
   113	    (complete M good a₀).effect a =
   114	      M.effect a + if a = a₀ then badEffect M good else 0 := by
   115	  classical
   116	  rw [complete, Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter]
   117	  have hterm (b : α) :
   118	      (if toGood good a₀ b = a then M.effect b else 0) =
   119	        (if b = a.val then M.effect b else 0) +
   120	          if a = a₀ then (if ¬ good b then M.effect b else 0) else 0 := by
   121	    by_cases hb : good b
   122	    · have heq : toGood good a₀ b = a ↔ b = a.val := by
   123	        simp [toGood, hb, Subtype.ext_iff]
   124	      simp [heq, hb]
   125	    · have hba : b ≠ a.val := by
   126	        rintro rfl
   127	        exact hb a.property
   128	      simp [toGood, hb, hba, eq_comm]
   129	  simp_rw [hterm]
   130	  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   131	  simp [badEffect, Finset.sum_filter, Finset.sum_ite_irrel]
   132	
   133	/-- Relabeling the completed measurement adds the bad effect to exactly the
   134	label of the chosen default outcome, relative to the relabeled restriction. -/
   135	theorem complete_postprocess_effect (M : Measurement α ι)
   136	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (a₀ : {a // good a})
   137	    (g : {a // good a} → β) (b : β) :
   138	    ((complete M good a₀).postprocess g).effect b =
   139	      ((restrict M good).postprocess g).effect b +
   140	        if b = g a₀ then badEffect M good else 0 := by
   141	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   142	  simp_rw [complete_effect]
   143	  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   144	  congr 1
   145	  simp [eq_comm]

   147	private theorem postprocess_overlap (M : Measurement α ι) (N : Measurement β ι)
   148	    (f : α → β) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   149	    (∑ b, stateQForm ψ ((M.postprocess f).effect b * N.effect b)) =
   150	      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ (M.effect a * N.effect (f a)) := by
   151	  simp only [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_mul,
   152	    stateQForm_finset_sum]
   153	  calc
   154	    (∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b),
   155	        stateQForm ψ (M.effect a * N.effect b)) =
   156	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b),
   157	        stateQForm ψ (M.effect a * N.effect (f a)) := by
   158	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   159	          intro b _
   160	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   161	          intro a ha
   162	          rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2]
   163	    _ = _ := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f _
   164	
   165	private theorem postprocess_defect (μ : Distribution X) (M : Measurement α ι)
   166	    (N : X → Measurement β ι) (f : X → α → β) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   167	    consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => (M.postprocess (f x)).effect a)
   168	        (fun x a => (N x).effect a) ψ =
   169	      avgOver μ (fun x => ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 -
   170	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ (M.effect a * (N x).effect (f x a))) := by
   171	  unfold consistencyDefect
   172	  simp_rw [consistency_term_eq_stateQForm, point_defect_eq, postprocess_overlap]
   173	
   174	private theorem leftPlaced_postprocess (M : Measurement α ιA) (f : α → β) :
   175	    leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := ιB) (M.postprocess f) =
   176	      (leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := ιB) M).postprocess f := by
   177	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
   178	  intro b
   179	  exact heteroKron_finset_sum_left _ _ _
   180	
   181	private theorem rightPlaced_postprocess (M : Measurement α ιB) (f : α → β) :
   182	    rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := ιA) (M.postprocess f) =
   183	      (rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := ιA) M).postprocess f := by
   184	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
   185	  intro b
   186	  exact heteroKron_finset_sum_right _ _ _

   188	private theorem left_postprocess_defect (μ : Distribution X) (M : Measurement α ιA)
   189	    (N : X → Measurement β ιB) (f : X → α → β)
   190	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   191	    consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => heteroKron ((M.postprocess (f x)).effect a) 1)
   192	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect a)) ψ =
   193	      avgOver μ (fun x => ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 -
   194	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (M.effect a) ((N x).effect (f x a)))) := by
   195	  change consistencyDefect μ
   196	    (fun x a => (leftPlacedMeasurement (M.postprocess (f x))).effect a)
   197	    (fun x a => (rightPlacedMeasurement (N x)).effect a) ψ = _
   198	  simp_rw [leftPlaced_postprocess]
   199	  rw [postprocess_defect]
   200	  simp only [leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement,
   201	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne, placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   202	
   203	private theorem right_postprocess_defect (μ : Distribution X) (M : Measurement α ιB)
   204	    (N : X → Measurement β ιA) (f : X → α → β)
   205	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   206	    consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((M.postprocess (f x)).effect a))
   207	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((N x).effect a) 1) ψ =
   208	      avgOver μ (fun x => ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 -
   209	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ (heteroKron ((N x).effect (f x a)) (M.effect a))) := by
   210	  change consistencyDefect μ
   211	    (fun x a => (rightPlacedMeasurement (M.postprocess (f x))).effect a)
   212	    (fun x a => (leftPlacedMeasurement (N x)).effect a) ψ = _
   213	  simp_rw [rightPlaced_postprocess]
   214	  rw [postprocess_defect]
   215	  simp only [leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement,
   216	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne, heteroKron_mul, one_mul, mul_one]

   218	omit [DecidableEq α] [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] in
   219	/-- Equal good-outcome contributions cancel; the remaining averaged change
   220	is bounded by the sum of the bad-outcome upper bounds. -/
   221	private theorem abs_avg_sum_change_le (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
   222	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (u v : X → α → ℝ) (r : α → ℝ)
   223	    (hu : ∀ x a, 0 ≤ u x a ∧ u x a ≤ r a)
   224	    (hv : ∀ x a, 0 ≤ v x a ∧ v x a ≤ r a)
   225	    (huv : ∀ x a, good a → u x a = v x a) (c : ℝ) :
   226	    |avgOver μ (fun x => c - ∑ a, u x a) -
   227	        avgOver μ (fun x => c - ∑ a, v x a)| ≤
   228	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => ¬ good a), r a := by
   229	  have hpoint (x : X) :
   230	      |(c - ∑ a, u x a) - (c - ∑ a, v x a)| ≤
   231	        ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => ¬ good a), r a := by
   232	    have hterm (a : α) : |v x a - u x a| ≤ if ¬ good a then r a else 0 := by
   233	      by_cases ha : good a
   234	      · simp [ha, huv x a ha]
   235	      · rw [if_pos ha]
   236	        exact abs_le.mpr ⟨by linarith [(hu x a).2, (hv x a).1],
   237	          by linarith [(hv x a).2, (hu x a).1]⟩
   238	    calc
   239	      _ = |∑ a, (v x a - u x a)| := by
   240	        rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   241	        congr 1
   242	        ring
   243	      _ ≤ ∑ a, |v x a - u x a| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
   244	      _ ≤ ∑ a, if ¬ good a then r a else 0 :=
   245	        Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => hterm a
   246	      _ = _ := (Finset.sum_filter _ _).symm
   247	  rw [← avgOver_sub]
   248	  calc
   249	    _ ≤ avgOver μ (fun x => |(c - ∑ a, u x a) - (c - ∑ a, v x a)|) := by
   250	      unfold avgOver
   251	      refine (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans_eq ?_
   252	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   253	      intro x _
   254	      rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (μ.nonnegative x)]
   255	    _ ≤ avgOver μ (fun _ =>
   256	        ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => ¬ good a), r a) :=
   257	      avgOver_mono μ _ _ hpoint
   258	    _ = _ := avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ _
   259	
   260	/-- Relabelings that agree on good outcomes change Alice-first cross-player
   261	consistency by at most Alice's bad-outcome state mass. The spaces may differ,
   262	the other measurement need not be projective, and the state may be unnormalized.
   263	This auxiliary isolates the quantitative content of the source completion step. -/
   264	theorem abs_postprocess_consistency_left_sub_le
   265	    (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (M : Measurement α ιA)
   266	    (N : X → Measurement β ιB) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
   267	    (f g : X → α → β) (hfg : ∀ x a, good a → f x a = g x a)
   268	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   269	    |consistencyDefect μ
   270	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((M.postprocess (f x)).effect a) 1)
   271	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect a)) ψ -
   272	      consistencyDefect μ
   273	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((M.postprocess (g x)).effect a) 1)
   274	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect a)) ψ| ≤
   275	      stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (badEffect M good) (1 : Op ιB)) := by
   276	  rw [left_postprocess_defect, left_postprocess_defect]
   277	  simp only [badEffect, heteroKron_finset_sum_left, stateQForm_finset_sum]
   278	  have hbound (x : X) (a : α) (b : β) :
   279	      0 ≤ stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (M.effect a) ((N x).effect b)) ∧
   280	        stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (M.effect a) ((N x).effect b)) ≤
   281	          stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (M.effect a) (1 : Op ιB)) :=
   282	    ⟨stateQForm_nonneg ψ (kronecker_nonneg (M.pos a) ((N x).pos b)),
   283	      quadratic_form_mono
   284	        (kronecker_le_kronecker_right_one (M.pos a) (measurement_effect_le_one (N x) b)) ψ⟩
   285	  exact abs_avg_sum_change_le μ hμ good _ _ _
   286	    (fun x a => hbound x a (f x a)) (fun x a => hbound x a (g x a))
   287	    (fun x a ha => by rw [hfg x a ha]) _
   288	
   289	/-- Relabelings that agree on good outcomes change Bob-first cross-player
   290	consistency by at most Bob's bad-outcome state mass. The completed measurement
   291	is the first consistency argument, although it acts on the right tensor factor;
   292	this is the orientation of the Bob conclusion of `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
   293	theorem abs_postprocess_consistency_right_sub_le
   294	    (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (M : Measurement α ιB)
   295	    (N : X → Measurement β ιA) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
   296	    (f g : X → α → β) (hfg : ∀ x a, good a → f x a = g x a)
   297	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   298	    |consistencyDefect μ
   299	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((M.postprocess (f x)).effect a))
   300	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((N x).effect a) 1) ψ -
   301	      consistencyDefect μ
   302	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((M.postprocess (g x)).effect a))
   303	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((N x).effect a) 1) ψ| ≤
   304	      stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) (badEffect M good)) := by
   305	  rw [right_postprocess_defect, right_postprocess_defect]
   306	  simp only [badEffect, heteroKron_finset_sum_right, stateQForm_finset_sum]
   307	  have hbound (x : X) (a : α) (b : β) :
   308	      0 ≤ stateQForm ψ (heteroKron ((N x).effect b) (M.effect a)) ∧
   309	        stateQForm ψ (heteroKron ((N x).effect b) (M.effect a)) ≤
   310	          stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) (M.effect a)) :=
   311	    ⟨stateQForm_nonneg ψ (kronecker_nonneg ((N x).pos b) (M.pos a)),
   312	      quadratic_form_mono
   313	        (kronecker_mono_left (measurement_effect_le_one (N x) b) (M.pos a)) ψ⟩
   314	  exact abs_avg_sum_change_le μ hμ good _ _ _
   315	    (fun x a => hbound x a (f x a)) (fun x a => hbound x a (g x a))
   316	    (fun x a ha => by rw [hfg x a ha]) _
   317	
   318	/-- After any outcome maps agreeing on the good outcomes, the constructed
   319	completion changes Alice-first consistency by at most the bad projection's
   320	state mass. Together with `complete_isProjective`, this is the finite-measurement
   321	adapter for the completion step of `lem:qld-4-7`, not its source mass estimate. -/
   322	theorem abs_complete_consistency_left_sub_le
   323	    (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (M : Measurement α ιA)
   324	    (N : X → Measurement β ιB) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
   325	    (a₀ : {a // good a}) (f : X → α → β) (g : X → {a // good a} → β)
   326	    (hgf : ∀ x a, g x a = f x a) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   327	    |consistencyDefect μ
   328	        (fun x a => heteroKron (((complete M good a₀).postprocess (g x)).effect a) 1)
   329	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect a)) ψ -
   330	      consistencyDefect μ
   331	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((M.postprocess (f x)).effect a) 1)
   332	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect a)) ψ| ≤
   333	      stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (badEffect M good) (1 : Op ιB)) := by
   334	  simp only [complete, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_comp]
   335	  apply abs_postprocess_consistency_left_sub_le μ hμ M N good _ f _ ψ
   336	  intro x a ha
   337	  simpa only [toGood, dif_pos ha] using hgf x ⟨a, ha⟩
   338	
   339	/-- The same completion estimate with the completed measurement on Bob's
   340	space, still as the first argument of consistency. Both player spaces and the
   341	order of the tensor factors remain explicit. -/
   342	theorem abs_complete_consistency_right_sub_le
   343	    (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (M : Measurement α ιB)
   344	    (N : X → Measurement β ιA) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
   345	    (a₀ : {a // good a}) (f : X → α → β) (g : X → {a // good a} → β)
   346	    (hgf : ∀ x a, g x a = f x a) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   347	    |consistencyDefect μ
   348	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (((complete M good a₀).postprocess (g x)).effect a))
   349	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((N x).effect a) 1) ψ -
   350	      consistencyDefect μ
   351	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((M.postprocess (f x)).effect a))
   352	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((N x).effect a) 1) ψ| ≤
   353	      stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) (badEffect M good)) := by
   354	  simp only [complete, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_comp]
   355	  apply abs_postprocess_consistency_right_sub_le μ hμ M N good _ f _ ψ
   356	  intro x a ha
   357	  simpa only [toGood, dif_pos ha] using hgf x ⟨a, ha⟩
   358	
   359	/-- Adding one fixed operator at a question-dependent outcome changes the
   360	defect by its total state mass minus the overlap at that outcome. -/
   361	private theorem add_at_outcome_defect (μ : Distribution X)
   362	    (A : X → β → Op ι) (N : X → Measurement β ι)
   363	    (R : Op ι) (k : X → β) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   364	    consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => A x a + if a = k x then R else 0)
   365	        (fun x a => (N x).effect a) ψ =
   366	      consistencyDefect μ A (fun x a => (N x).effect a) ψ +
   367	        avgOver μ (fun x => stateQForm ψ R - stateQForm ψ (R * (N x).effect (k x))) := by
   368	  unfold consistencyDefect
   369	  simp_rw [consistency_term_eq_stateQForm]
   370	  have hpoint (x : X) :
   371	      (∑ a, ∑ b, if a = b then 0 else
   372	        stateQForm ψ ((A x a + if a = k x then R else 0) * (N x).effect b)) =
   373	      (∑ a, ∑ b, if a = b then 0 else stateQForm ψ (A x a * (N x).effect b)) +
   374	        (stateQForm ψ R - stateQForm ψ (R * (N x).effect (k x))) := by
   375	    have hterm (a b : β) :
   376	        (if a = b then 0 else
   377	          stateQForm ψ ((A x a + if a = k x then R else 0) * (N x).effect b)) =
   378	        (if a = b then 0 else stateQForm ψ (A x a * (N x).effect b)) +
   379	          if a = k x then
   380	            (if a = b then 0 else stateQForm ψ (R * (N x).effect b)) else 0 := by
   381	      by_cases hab : a = b
   382	      · simp only [hab, if_true, ite_self, add_zero]
   383	      · simp only [hab, if_false]
   384	        by_cases ha : a = k x <;> simp [ha, add_mul, stateQForm_add]
   385	    simp_rw [hterm, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   386	    congr 1
   387	    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   388	    simp only [Finset.sum_ite_eq', Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
   389	    rw [Finset.sum_ite]
   390	    simp only [Finset.sum_const_zero, zero_add]
   391	    rw [show Finset.univ.filter (fun b => ¬ k x = b) = Finset.univ.erase (k x) by
   392	      ext b
   393	      simp [ne_comm]]
   394	    rw [Finset.sum_erase_eq_sub (Finset.mem_univ _),
   395	      ← stateQForm_finset_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum,
   396	      (N x).sum_eq_one, mul_one]

   398	  exact avgOver_add μ _ _
   399	
   400	/-- Completing the good restriction and then relabeling increases Alice-first
   401	consistency by at most the bad-effect mass. This directly applies to the
   402	submeasurement relation preceding completion in the source; projectivity of the
   403	constructed complete measurement is supplied by `complete_isProjective`. -/
   404	theorem complete_restrict_consistency_left_le
   405	    (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (M : Measurement α ιA)
   406	    (N : X → Measurement β ιB) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
   407	    (a₀ : {a // good a}) (g : X → {a // good a} → β)
   408	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   409	    consistencyDefect μ
   410	        (fun x a => heteroKron (((complete M good a₀).postprocess (g x)).effect a) 1)
   411	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect a)) ψ ≤
   412	      consistencyDefect μ
   413	        (fun x a => heteroKron (((restrict M good).postprocess (g x)).effect a) 1)
   414	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect a)) ψ +
   415	      stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (badEffect M good) (1 : Op ιB)) := by
   416	  have heffect (x : X) (a : β) :
   417	      heteroKron (((complete M good a₀).postprocess (g x)).effect a) (1 : Op ιB) =
   418	        heteroKron (((restrict M good).postprocess (g x)).effect a) 1 +
   419	          if a = g x a₀ then heteroKron (badEffect M good) 1 else 0 := by
   420	    rw [complete_postprocess_effect, heteroKron_add_left]
   421	    by_cases h : a = g x a₀ <;> simp [h, heteroKron]
   422	  simp_rw [heffect]
   423	  have hdefect := add_at_outcome_defect μ
   424	    (fun x a => heteroKron (((restrict M good).postprocess (g x)).effect a) 1)
   425	    (fun x => rightPlacedMeasurement (N x))
   426	    (heteroKron (badEffect M good) 1) (fun x => g x a₀) ψ
   427	  dsimp only [rightPlacedMeasurement, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne] at hdefect
   428	  rw [hdefect]
   429	  apply add_le_add le_rfl
   430	  calc
   431	    _ ≤ avgOver μ (fun _ => stateQForm ψ
   432	        (heteroKron (badEffect M good) (1 : Op ιB))) := by
   433	      apply avgOver_mono
   434	      intro x
   435	      apply sub_le_self
   436	      change 0 ≤ stateQForm ψ
   437	        (heteroKron (badEffect M good) 1 * heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect (g x a₀)))
   438	      rw [placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   439	      exact stateQForm_nonneg ψ (kronecker_nonneg (badEffect_nonneg M good) ((N x).pos _))
   440	    _ = _ := avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ _
   441	
   442	/-- The direct restriction-to-completion estimate with the completed
   443	measurement on Bob's space and first in the consistency relation. -/
   444	theorem complete_restrict_consistency_right_le
   445	    (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (M : Measurement α ιB)
   446	    (N : X → Measurement β ιA) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
   447	    (a₀ : {a // good a}) (g : X → {a // good a} → β)
   448	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   449	    consistencyDefect μ
   450	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (((complete M good a₀).postprocess (g x)).effect a))
   451	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((N x).effect a) 1) ψ ≤
   452	      consistencyDefect μ
   453	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (((restrict M good).postprocess (g x)).effect a))
   454	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((N x).effect a) 1) ψ +
   455	      stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) (badEffect M good)) := by
   456	  have heffect (x : X) (a : β) :
   457	      heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) (((complete M good a₀).postprocess (g x)).effect a) =
   458	        heteroKron 1 (((restrict M good).postprocess (g x)).effect a) +
   459	          if a = g x a₀ then heteroKron 1 (badEffect M good) else 0 := by
   460	    rw [complete_postprocess_effect, heteroKron_add_right]
   461	    by_cases h : a = g x a₀ <;> simp [h, heteroKron]
   462	  simp_rw [heffect]
   463	  have hdefect := add_at_outcome_defect μ
   464	    (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (((restrict M good).postprocess (g x)).effect a))
   465	    (fun x => leftPlacedMeasurement (N x))
   466	    (heteroKron 1 (badEffect M good)) (fun x => g x a₀) ψ
   467	  dsimp only [leftPlacedMeasurement, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne] at hdefect
   468	  rw [hdefect]
   469	  apply add_le_add le_rfl
   470	  calc
   471	    _ ≤ avgOver μ (fun _ => stateQForm ψ
   472	        (heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) (badEffect M good))) := by
   473	      apply avgOver_mono
   474	      intro x
   475	      apply sub_le_self
   476	      change 0 ≤ stateQForm ψ
   477	        (heteroKron 1 (badEffect M good) * heteroKron ((N x).effect (g x a₀)) 1)
   478	      rw [heteroKron_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
   479	      exact stateQForm_nonneg ψ (kronecker_nonneg ((N x).pos _) (badEffect_nonneg M good))
   480	    _ = _ := avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ _

     3	/-!
     4	# Evaluation on a nondegenerate affine line
     5	
     6	This module identifies completed line-polynomial evaluation with evaluation at
     7	the unique affine parameter of a point on a line with nonzero direction.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The result is the geometric step in the collision argument at
    12	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.

    21	/-- On a nonzero direction, completed evaluation agrees with polynomial
    22	evaluation at the unique affine parameter. -/
    23	theorem evalOpt_affine_parameter_of_direction_ne_zero {L : LdParams}
    24	    {bound : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L) (hdir : line.direction ≠ 0)
    25	    (poly : DegPoly L bound) (param : ScalarQ L) :
    26	    evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) poly =
    27	      some (evalCoefficient poly param) := by
    28	  apply WinImplications.evalOpt_eq_some_of_evaluatesTo
    29	  refine ⟨⟨param, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
    30	  intro other heq
    31	  have hsmul : param • line.direction = other • line.direction :=
    32	    add_left_cancel heq
    33	  have hsub : (param - other) • line.direction = 0 := by
    34	    rw [sub_smul, hsmul, sub_self]
    35	  have hparam : param = other :=
    36	    sub_eq_zero.mp ((smul_eq_zero.mp hsub).resolve_right hdir)
    37	  rw [hparam]
    38	
    39	end

    25	/-- Resampling a uniform affine parameter on the sampled axis line preserves

    29	    (value : (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) → ℝ) :
    30	    avgOver (aLinePointDist L) value =
    31	    avgOver (aLinePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    32	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    33	        value (sample.1, sample.1.base + param • sample.1.direction))) := by

    40	  rw [uniformDistribution_prod]
    41	  simp only [avgOver_prod]
    42	  rw [avgOver_comm, avgOver_comm (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))]

    55	      (fun point => lineValue (lineRepMap direction point) point)) hmap

    61	      value (LineDesc.axis (lineRepMap direction point) block.1
    62	        (lineRepMap_apply_self direction point), point)) =
    63	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) (fun point =>
    64	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    65	        value (LineDesc.axis (lineRepMap direction point) block.1
    66	          (lineRepMap_apply_self direction point),
    67	          lineRepMap direction point + param • direction)))

    70	      (lineRepMap direction base) block.1

    15	The collision estimate supports `lem:qld-xz-lines` at
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963` and

    27	/-- The concrete nondegenerate line-pasting distribution satisfies the
    28	conditional collision bound required by `lem:pasting`. This is the
    29	formalization-only Schwartz--Zippel conditioning auxiliary used in
    30	`lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper lines 950--963. -/
    31	theorem nondegenerateLinePastingDist_collision_bound
    32	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (bound : ℕ) :
    33	    HasConditionalCollisionBound (nondegenerateLinePastingDist P.toLdParams)
    34	      (fun (poly : DegPoly P.toLdParams bound) sample => evalOpt sample.1 sample.2 poly)

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditional collision bounds from fiber averages
     5	
     6	This module converts an unnormalized collision estimate on every first-question
     7	fiber into the positive-mass conditional collision predicate used by the
     8	pasting theorem.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The conditional collision hypothesis is from `lem:pasting`,
    13	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`. Its use in
    14	the QPBT combining argument occurs at
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	noncomputable section
    25	
    26	/-- An unnormalized collision estimate on every first-question fiber implies
    27	the positive-mass conditional collision predicate of `lem:pasting`. This is a
    28	formalization-only normalization adapter for paper lines 504--525. -/
    29	theorem collision_bound_of_fiber_averages {X Y₁ Y₂ R₂ Γ₂ : Type*}
    30	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y₁] [DecidableEq Y₁]
    31	    [Fintype Y₂] [DecidableEq Y₂] [Fintype R₂] [DecidableEq R₂]
    32	    [Fintype Γ₂] (dist : Distribution ((X × Y₁) × Y₂))
    33	    (eval₂ : Γ₂ → Y₂ → R₂) (eta : ℝ)
    34	    (hbound : ∀ fixed : X × Y₁, ∀ first second : Γ₂, first ≠ second →
    35	      avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = fixed then
    36	        (if eval₂ first sample.2 = eval₂ second sample.2 then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
    37	      eta * avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = fixed then 1 else 0)) :
    38	    HasConditionalCollisionBound dist eval₂ eta := by
    39	  classical
    40	  intro question point _ first second hne
    41	  have havg (value : ((X × Y₁) × Y₂) → ℝ) :
    42	      avgOver dist value = ∑ sample, dist.weight sample * value sample := by
    43	    exact (dist.sum_univ_eq_sum_support _ (fun sample hout => by
    44	      rw [dist.outsideSupport sample hout, zero_mul])).symm
    45	  have hmass : (dist.map Prod.fst).weight (question, point) =
    46	      avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = (question, point) then 1 else 0) := by
    47	    rw [Distribution.map_weight]
    48	    unfold avgOver
    49	    rw [Finset.sum_filter]
    50	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    51	    intro sample _
    52	    by_cases hfixed : sample.1 = (question, point) <;> simp [hfixed]
    53	  rw [hmass]
    54	  have h := hbound (question, point) first second hne
    55	  simpa [havg, Fintype.sum_prod_type, mul_ite] using h
    56	
    57	end
    58	
    59	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

# Blueprint Style Guide & Lessons Learned

## Core Philosophy
The blueprint is a **bridge between the mathematics and the Lean formalization**. A reader should be able to read a blueprint entry and immediately understand the corresponding Lean declaration. Conversely, someone reading the Lean code should find the blueprint proof sketch faithful to what the code actually does.

## General Principles
1. **Blueprint ↔ Lean must match.** Every `\lean{X}` tag must correspond to an actual Lean declaration. Every proof sketch must match what the Lean proof actually does — not a hand-wavy version of it.
2. **Standalone.** `blueprint/` and any slides are independent — no cross-references, no shared files. Each has its own macros, its own `references.bib`.
3. **Mathematical language only — zero Lean jargon.** No Lean identifiers in prose (no `selfImprovement_step`, no `PastingLemma.aux`, no `rintro ⟨X, hX⟩`). The `\lean{...}` tag is the link; the body text is standard mathematics. If you can't say it in math, rewrite it.
4. **No filler prose.** Only precise definitions, theorem statements, and proof sketches. No "this is important because..." or "the self-improvement step governs the induction...".
5. **Cite non-trivial things.** Basic definitions don't need citations. Important results and non-obvious definitions should cite the source paper.
6. **Don't invent terminology or notation.** Don't create ad-hoc notation when standard notation exists. Don't name things that the literature doesn't name.
7. **Match Lean's theorem/lemma/def exactly.** If Lean says `theorem X`, use `\begin{theorem}`. If Lean says `lemma X`, use `\begin{lemma}`. `\begin{proposition}` is allowed in blueprint prose when it improves mathematical readability, but still map it to an actual Lean `theorem`/`lemma` declaration via `\lean{...}`. Label prefix: `thm:` for theorem, `lem:` for lemma, `def:` for definition, `prop:` for proposition.

### Remark On Mathematical Prose

Blueprint entries should read as mathematical exposition, not as progress
reports. The mathematical argument should determine the order of the prose:
introduce the notation, state the assertion, give the proof or calculation, and
then record Lean references through the usual blueprint tags. Lean declarations,
file paths, and proof-status information should not become the visible structure
of the paragraph. When referring to a source article, cite it bibliographically
rather than relying on an uncited reference to the article.

Use displayed formulae when the formula benefits from visual separation, and
keep short scalar definitions or elementary inequalities inline when the
sentence reads better that way. As in ordinary mathematical writing, displayed
formulae should be punctuated as part of the sentences in which they occur.

## Proof Sketches Must Match Lean
This is the most important rule. Every proof in the blueprint must faithfully describe what the Lean proof does:

- **Reference the actual lemmas used.** If the Lean proof calls `LDT.selfImprovement`, the blueprint proof should say "By Lemma X.Y (self-improvement)..." and list it in `\uses`.
- **Do not use `\cref` or `\Cref`.** The blueprint does not load `cleveref`.
  Spell out the kind of object and use ordinary references, for example
  `Lemma~\ref{lem:self-improvement}` or `Theorem~\ref{thm:main-formal}`.
- **Describe the actual proof structure.** If Lean does induction on a parameter, say so. If Lean uses a specific decomposition, name it.
- **Don't hand-wave where Lean is specific.** "Standard argument" is not acceptable if Lean uses three specific lemmas. Name them.
- **Don't be more specific than Lean.** If Lean uses `simp` to close a goal, a one-line sketch is fine.
- **`\uses` in proofs must be accurate.** Only list what the proof actually uses, not what the statement mentions.

## Source-Labelled Statements And Conditional Helpers

If a blueprint theorem, lemma, or proposition carries a source label from the
paper, the linked Lean declaration must state the same theorem, up to faithful
formal encoding of the paper's domain.  Do not use `\lean{...}` and `\leanok`
on the source-labelled statement to point to a conditional helper whose
additional assumptions supply an unproved part of the paper proof.
Changing the Lean statement away from `references/ldt-paper/` is strongly
discouraged unless faithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical
necessity requires it; the blueprint should make any such necessity explicit.

Boundary hypotheses such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
positivity of parameters, and denominator nonvanishing may be faithful when
they express the mathematical domain that the paper leaves implicit.  By
contrast, bridge inputs, residual data, repair hypotheses, producer
assumptions, proof-obligation inputs, or package assumptions are proof debt.
They must not be added to a source-labelled theorem statement.  If such data is
still unproved, the source-labelled Lean theorem should keep the source-shaped
statement and carry a tracked `sorry`, or the missing assertion should appear
as the lowest named internal obligation with a tracked `sorry`.  A separately
named conditional helper should not be introduced as a repair pattern.  If one
already contains substantial proof content, it may remain temporarily only as
quarantine: it needs a paper source, a tracking issue, and a discharge or
deletion plan.  The blueprint should leave the paper theorem unmarked as
proof-complete until the source-faithful Lean statement has a source-faithful
proof.

If a Lean theorem proves only a restricted version of a source theorem, the
blueprint entry carrying `\leanok` must state that restriction in the theorem
statement itself.  It must not be cited as the unrestricted source theorem.
When the only Lean declaration available for a source label has extra
non-paper assumptions, remove the `\leanok` claim from the source-labelled
entry or move the restricted statement to a separate Lean-only entry.  The
unrestricted paper theorem remains unformalized until a Lean statement with
the source's hypothesis set exists.

## Notation Consistency
Notation must be **internally consistent** across the entire blueprint and **close to what the Lean code expresses**:

- **Indices**: 0-indexed where matching `Fin n` in Lean
- **Finite fields / alphabets**: use standard notation for the alphabet $\Sigma$ and finite fields $\mathbb{F}_q$
- **Measurements**: use standard quantum measurement notation (projective measurements, POVMs)
- **Strategies**: quantum strategies for nonlocal games should use standard notation from the literature
- **Expansion**: use standard notation for graph expansion parameters
- **Macros** (in `macros/common.tex`): define project-specific macros and use them consistently

The original reference controls notation whenever it gives a usable convention.
If the blueprint needs a different symbol, index convention, or name in order to
match Lean, introduce it explicitly and relate it to the paper notation in the
same paragraph.  Do not let a `\lean{...}` tag, a Lean namespace, or a file name
be the only explanation of a changed term.

When a public Lean declaration is a formalization-only auxiliary lemma, the
blueprint should say so before listing the declaration.  The surrounding prose
should identify the paper theorem, equation, or construction that the auxiliary
lemma supports, and should avoid making the auxiliary name look like a named
result from the source article.

## What NOT to Put in the Blueprint
- **Lean identifier names in math text.** Write "the self-improvement lemma", never "the `selfImprovement` step". The `\lean{LDT.selfImprovement}` tag handles the linking.
- **Implementation details.** Don't say "bundled as an element of the Euclidean space" or "using `EuclideanSpace.equiv`". Describe the mathematical object.
- **Ad-hoc notation.** Don't invent superscripts or subscripts to distinguish from existing notation. Use standard conventions.
- **Function-call syntax.** Use mathematical notation, not programming notation.
- **Redundant definitions.** If two blueprint definitions describe the same mathematical object, consolidate them. Each definition should introduce genuinely new mathematical content.
- **Lean namespace prefixes in prose.** Don't write "the `LDT.PastingLemma`" — write "the pasting lemma".

## Banned AI/Software Language (enforced in both blueprint AND Lean code)
The blueprint reads as a **mathematical document**, not software documentation. The following patterns are banned in ALL reader-facing text (section titles, theorem names, proof sketches, remarks, chapter preambles) and in ALL Lean docstrings, comments, and section names:

### Banned terms → replacements:
| Banned | Use instead |
|--------|------------|
| "Assembly" (as section/chapter title) | "Proof of [theorem]", "Construction", "Composition" |
| "Pipeline" | "reduction", "construction", "proof chain" |
| "Bridge" (as noun for a connection) | "connection", name by mathematical content |
| "Handoff" / "hand off" | "transition", "continuation", or drop entirely |
| "In this blueprint" / "Within this blueprint" | "here", "in what follows", or omit |
| "Honest" (as adjective for rigorous) | "exact", "faithful", "unconditional", "complete" |
| "Glue layer" | "intermediate construction", "connecting results" |
| "Re-export" / "reexport" | "provides", "re-states" |
| "Wiring" / "wire up" | "connecting", "composing", "combining" |
| "Package" (as noun for a data bundle) | "form", "data", "structure" |
| "Sorry-free" | acceptable only in Lean-specific technical context |

### Additional rules:
- **Section names in Lean**: use mathematical terms (`section QuantumSoundness`, `section SelfImprovement`, `section PastingLemma`), not organizational terms (`section Assembly`, `section Pipeline`).
- **Internal LaTeX labels** (e.g., `\label{ch:soundness}`) are not reader-facing and need not be renamed if doing so would break cross-references. But NEW labels should follow the standard.
- **Definitions that are actually theorems**: if a statement asserts a mathematical fact, it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not `\begin{definition}`. Definitions introduce new objects; theorems prove properties.

## `\uses` Dependency Guidelines
- **Statement `\uses`**: list only what's needed to *state* the result (typically definitions of the objects involved). Keep minimal — transitive deps are automatic.
- **Proof `\uses`**: list only what the proof *actually calls*. Don't list definitions unless the proof unfolds that definition.
- **Never self-reference**: a proof's `\uses` must NOT include the label of the theorem it proves.

## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas
Some Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements
from the original papers. These must be traceable without making the blueprint
look as if the paper stated them.

- If a declaration directly formalizes a paper or blueprint statement, record
  it as usual with `\lean{...}` on that statement and cite the relevant source.
- If a public declaration is an auxiliary lemma introduced only for the Lean
  proof, make that status explicit. Its Lean docstring should say that it is a
  formalization-only auxiliary lemma and should name the nearby paper equation,
  anchored paper passage, or blueprint label it supports. Blueprint line
  ranges are derived review context, not stored docstring citations; resolve a
  label with `python3 scripts/blueprint_citations.py resolve <label>`.
- If such an auxiliary declaration is important enough to be referenced from
  the blueprint, give it a clearly subordinate blueprint node, for example
  `[Formalization support for ...]`, and state in the first sentence that the
  lemma is not a named statement of the paper but isolates a step used in the
  Lean proof.
- Connect auxiliary nodes to the corresponding result from the paper with `\uses{...}` from
  the proof that actually calls them. Do not add them only to silence a sync
  warning; the dependency edge should explain where the auxiliary result is
  used.
- Do not mark an auxiliary node with proof-level `\leanok` unless its Lean proof
  is complete and `#print axioms` has no `sorryAx`. Statement-level `\leanok`
  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the
  proof remains tracked as incomplete.

## Blueprint Structure
- `content.tex` is a router: `\input{chapter/ch01_intro}` etc.
- Each chapter is a separate file in `chapter/`
- Definitions/theorems numbered within chapters: `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[chapter]`

## Lean Blueprint Macros
- `\lean{Namespace.DeclName}` — links to Lean declaration
- `\leanok` — context-sensitive marker; see "Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`" below
- `\uses{label1, label2}` — declares dependency edges for the graph
- `\notready` — marks as not ready for formalization (orange in graph)
- `\mathlibok` — already in Mathlib (dark green in graph; see legend note below)

### Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`

`\leanok` is context-sensitive for human review and graph interpretation. The same macro is used for two different claims, so reviewers should read it by placement rather than by raw token count.

**Statement-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\lean{...}`. It says that the corresponding Lean declaration exists and that its statement matches the blueprint or paper statement. It does **not** say that the Lean proof already exists or is complete. For definitions, this is the only `\leanok` marker.

**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).

A theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary node is **fully formalized in Lean if and only if it has both markers**: statement-level `\leanok` in the statement block and proof-level `\leanok` in the proof block. Statement-level without proof-level means “the statement has been transcribed and matched, but the proof is not yet certified complete.” Definitions have no proof block, so statement-level `\leanok` alone is enough there.

Excerpt from `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`:

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Commutativity of the point measurements]\label{thm:commutativity-points}
  \lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.CommutativityPoints.commutativityPoints}
  \leanok
  \uses{def:good-strategy, def:approx_delta}
  Let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be an $(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  The strategy passes the diagonal lines test with probability $1-\gamma$.
\end{proof}
```

**Current CI behavior.** The advisory Blueprint ↔ Lean sync check in [`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`](ci-blueprint-sync.md) distinguishes the two placements. Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.

`leanblueprint` does not use distinct macro names for these two claims, so audits must distinguish them by environment context rather than by raw `\leanok` counts. A future split such as `\leanokstmt` / `\leanokproof` could make that distinction explicit, but that is only a possible later cleanup; the current convention is to keep `\leanok` and rely on placement.

A recurring historical example is the chapter 4 `Q/X/\widehat X/P` witness
layer.  Once Lean has construction theorems deriving the displayed identities
and estimates from the rank-reduction, sigma-range, positive-Gram, native
spectral-theorem, or rectangular-SVD hypotheses, the corresponding blueprint
entries may carry `\leanok`.  A declaration that merely projects an identity
from an opaque data record is not enough by itself, and a theorem depending on
extra rectangular-SVD data should not be used as evidence for an unconditional
paper statement unless a separate construction supplies that data.

## Dependency Graph Colors (web)
- **Light green box**: definition with `\lean` + `\leanok` (defined in Lean)
- **Green**: theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary with `\lean` + statement-level `\leanok` (statement matched in Lean)
- **Dark green**: either (i) theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary with both statement-level and proof-level `\leanok` (fully formalized in Lean), or (ii) a `\mathlibok` node
- **Blue**: ready to state/prove (all deps are done)
- **Orange**: `\notready` (needs more blueprint work)

    32	    (t : ℝ) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1)
    33	    (μ ν : Distribution α) (f : α → ℝ) :
    34	    avgOver (Distribution.mix t ht0 ht1 μ ν) f =
    35	      t * avgOver μ f + (1 - t) * avgOver ν f := by
    36	  classical
    37	  unfold avgOver
    38	  have hsplit : (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support,
    39	        (t * μ.weight a + (1 - t) * ν.weight a) * f a) =
    40	      t * (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, μ.weight a * f a) +
    41	        (1 - t) * (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, ν.weight a * f a) := by
    42	    rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    43	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by ring
    44	  have hμ : (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, μ.weight a * f a) =
    45	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * f a := by
    46	    refine (Finset.sum_subset Finset.subset_union_left ?_).symm
    47	    intro a _ ha
    48	    rw [μ.outsideSupport a ha, zero_mul]
    49	  have hν : (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, ν.weight a * f a) =

    51	    refine (Finset.sum_subset Finset.subset_union_right ?_).symm
    52	    intro a _ ha

    54	  change (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support,
    55	    (t * μ.weight a + (1 - t) * ν.weight a) * f a) = _

    37	          evalOpt samples.1.1 samples.1.2 second then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤

    39	      avgOver (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)) (fun samples =>
    40	        if samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight samples.1.1 samples.2 else 0) := by

    42	  simp only [avgOver_prod]

    44	    (fun firstSample secondSample =>
    45	      if firstSample.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight firstSample.1 secondSample else 0)]

     4	/-!
     5	# Uniform collision bounds on nondegenerate affine lines
     6	
     7	This module combines uniqueness of affine evaluation with the univariate
     8	root-count bound to control collisions under a uniform line parameter.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The result is the Schwartz--Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
    13	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.
    14	-/
    15	
    16	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    17	
    18	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    19	
    20	noncomputable section
    21	
    22	/-- On a nondegenerate line, completed evaluations of distinct degree-bounded
    23	polynomials collide with probability at most the degree bound divided by the
    24	field size under a uniform affine parameter. -/
    25	theorem evalOpt_uniform_parameter_collision_le {L : LdParams} {bound : ℕ}
    26	    (line : LineDesc L) (hdir : line.direction ≠ 0)
    27	    (first second : DegPoly L bound) (hne : first ≠ second) :
    28	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    29	      if evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) first =
    30	        evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) second then 1 else 0) ≤
    31	      (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) := by
    32	  classical
    33	  simp_rw [evalOpt_affine_parameter_of_direction_ne_zero line hdir,
    34	    Option.some.injEq]
    35	  have hcard := evalCoefficient_collision_card_le first second hne
    36	  unfold avgOver
    37	  simp only [uniformDistribution_support, uniformDistribution_weight_apply,
    38	    mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero, ← Finset.sum_filter]
    39	  rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one_div]
    40	  exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (by exact_mod_cast hcard) (by positivity)
    41	
    42	end
    43	
    44	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Weighted collision bounds for sampled lines
     6	
     7	This module lifts the uniform affine-parameter collision estimate to the mixed
     8	line-point distribution with an arbitrary nonnegative weight depending only on
     9	the sampled line.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The estimate is the Schwartz--Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    20	
    21	noncomputable section
    22	
    23	/-- The collision bound remains valid with any nonnegative weight depending
    24	only on the line, after restricting to nonzero directions. This proof-only
    25	estimate is the conditional form of the root argument in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
    26	paper lines 950--955; it does not assert the false unrestricted collision bound
    27	on zero-direction coefficient presentations. -/
    28	theorem linePointDist_nondegenerate_weighted_collision_le {L : LdParams}
    29	    {bound : ℕ} (weight : LineDesc L → ℝ)
    30	    (hweight : ∀ line, 0 ≤ weight line) (first second : DegPoly L bound)
    31	    (hne : first ≠ second) :
    32	    avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    33	      if sample.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight sample.1 *
    34	        (if evalOpt sample.1 sample.2 first = evalOpt sample.1 sample.2 second
    35	          then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
    36	      (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) *
    37	        avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    38	          if sample.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight sample.1 else 0) := by
    39	  classical
    40	  rw [avgOver_linePointDist_resample_parameter]
    41	  rw [← avgOver_const_mul]
    42	  apply avgOver_mono
    43	  intro sample
    44	  by_cases hdir : sample.1.direction ≠ 0
    45	  · simp only [if_pos hdir]
    46	    rw [avgOver_const_mul]
    47	    exact (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
    48	      (evalOpt_uniform_parameter_collision_le sample.1 hdir first second hne)
    49	      (hweight sample.1)).trans_eq
    50	      (mul_comm _ _)
    51	  · simp [hdir, avgOver]
    52	
    53	end
    54	
    55	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Direct low-degree soundness for arbitrary strategies
     6	
     7	This module transports directly indexed low-degree soundness at simultaneity
     8	parameter `1` from projective strategies to arbitrary strategies. Both local
     9	measurement families are dilated by the existing one-measurement Naimark
    10	construction. The polynomial-tuple POVMs returned by projective soundness are
    11	then compressed to the original player carriers at the distinguished ancillary
    12	coordinate.
    13	
    14	Ground-slice compression preserves all three consistency defects exactly, so
    15	the error function and its universal constants are unchanged. The compressed
    16	polynomial POVMs are not asserted to be projective.
    17	
    18	## Main result
    19	
    20	* `exists_direct_ld_soundness_of_k_eq_one_any_strategy` removes the projectivity
    21	  premise from the formalization-only direct `k = 1` soundness route.
    22	
    23	## References
    24	
    25	The projective soundness input formalizes the shape of paper
    26	`lem:ld-soundness`,
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`.
    28	The Naimark transport supports the first paragraph of the proof of paper
    29	`lem:qld-4-7`,
    30	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1277-1289`.
    31	This module is Lean-only support and does not claim completion of that lemma.
    32	-/
    33	
    34	open scoped BigOperators
    35	
    36	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    37	
    38	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    39	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    40	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    41	
    42	noncomputable section
    43	
    44	/-- Dilate every direct-game question measurement and pad the bipartite state
    45	at the two distinguished `none` coordinates. -/
    46	private def directLdNaimarkStrategy (D : DirectLdParams)
    47	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) : Strategy (directLdGame D) :=
    48	  paddedStrategy S (none : Option (DirectLdAnswer D))
    49	    (none : Option (DirectLdAnswer D))
    50	    (fun question => dilatedMeasurement (default : DirectLdAnswer D) (S.A question))
    51	    (fun question => dilatedMeasurement (default : DirectLdAnswer D) (S.B question))
    52	
    53	/-- Every local measurement of the dilated direct-game strategy is projective. -/
    54	private theorem directLdNaimarkStrategy_isProjective (D : DirectLdParams)
    55	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) : (directLdNaimarkStrategy D S).IsProjective :=
    56	  paddedStrategy_isProjective S none none _ _
    57	    (fun question => dilatedMeasurement_isProjective
    58	      (default : DirectLdAnswer D) (S.A question))
    59	    (fun question => dilatedMeasurement_isProjective
    60	      (default : DirectLdAnswer D) (S.B question))
    61	
    62	/-- The direct-game value is unchanged by the two local Naimark dilations. -/
    63	private theorem directLdNaimarkStrategy_value (D : DirectLdParams)
    64	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) : (directLdNaimarkStrategy D S).value = S.value :=
    65	  paddedStrategy_value S none none _ _
    66	    (fun question answer => dilatedMeasurement_compression
    67	      (default : DirectLdAnswer D) answer (S.A question))
    68	    (fun question answer => dilatedMeasurement_compression
    69	      (default : DirectLdAnswer D) answer (S.B question))
    70	
    71	/-- Compressing Alice's dilated point measurement after point-answer
    72	postprocessing recovers the original postprocessed point measurement. -/
    73	private theorem directLdNaimarkStrategy_pointA_compress (D : DirectLdParams)
    74	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) (question : DirectLdQuestion D) :
    75	    (((directLdNaimarkStrategy D S).A question).postprocess
    76	        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).compressAt none =
    77	      (S.A question).postprocess (directLdPointValuesOrZero D) := by
    78	  change ((dilatedMeasurement (default : DirectLdAnswer D) (S.A question)).postprocess
    79	      (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).compressAt none = _
    80	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.compressAt_postprocess,
    81	    Measurement.compressAt_dilatedMeasurement]
    82	  rfl
    83	
    84	/-- Compressing Bob's dilated point measurement after point-answer
    85	postprocessing recovers the original postprocessed point measurement. -/
    86	private theorem directLdNaimarkStrategy_pointB_compress (D : DirectLdParams)
    87	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) (question : DirectLdQuestion D) :
    88	    (((directLdNaimarkStrategy D S).B question).postprocess
    89	        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).compressAt none =
    90	      (S.B question).postprocess (directLdPointValuesOrZero D) := by
    91	  change ((dilatedMeasurement (default : DirectLdAnswer D) (S.B question)).postprocess
    92	      (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).compressAt none = _
    93	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.compressAt_postprocess,
    94	    Measurement.compressAt_dilatedMeasurement]
    95	  rfl
    96	
    97	/-- Formalization-only soundness transport for the directly indexed low-degree
    98	game at simultaneity parameter `1`, with no projectivity premise on the input
    99	strategy.
   100	
   101	Apply Naimark dilation to both question-indexed POVM families, use
   102	`exists_direct_ld_soundness_of_k_eq_one` on the resulting projective strategy,
   103	and compress its two polynomial-tuple POVMs at the distinguished ancillary
   104	coordinates. The padded-state defect identity preserves the two point versus
   105	polynomial bounds and the polynomial self-consistency bound exactly, with the
   106	same witnesses `a`, `b`, and `deltaLd` as the projective theorem.
   107	
   108	This theorem is Lean-only support for the Naimark step in the proof of paper
   109	`lem:qld-4-7`,
   110	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1277-1289`.
   111	It does not assert projectivity of the compressed POVMs and introduces no
   112	premise for a paper-labelled QPBT producer. -/
   113	theorem exists_direct_ld_soundness_of_k_eq_one_any_strategy :
   114	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
   115	      ∀ (D : DirectLdParams) (ε : ℝ), D.k = 1 → 0 < ε →
   116	        ∀ S : Strategy (directLdGame D), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   117	          ∃ GA : DirectPolyMeasTuple D S.ιA,
   118	            ∃ GB : DirectPolyMeasTuple D S.ιB,
   119	              consistencyDefect
   120	                  (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   121	                  (fun u outcome =>
   122	                    heteroKron
   123	                      (((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
   124	                        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome) 1)
   125	                  (fun u outcome =>
   126	                    heteroKron 1
   127	                      ((GB.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
   128	                  S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε D.q D.m D.d D.k ∧
   129	              consistencyDefect
   130	                  (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   131	                  (fun u outcome =>
   132	                    heteroKron
   133	                      ((GA.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
   134	                  (fun u outcome =>
   135	                    heteroKron 1
   136	                      (((S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
   137	                        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome))
   138	                  S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε D.q D.m D.d D.k ∧
   139	              consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   140	                  (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   141	                  (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
   142	                  S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε D.q D.m D.d D.k := by

   144	  refine ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, ?_⟩

     4	/-!
     5	# Positivity of the consistency defect on opposite placements
     6	
     7	The error-inflation estimates for restricted line distributions apply to
     8	nonnegative averages.  This module supplies the missing nonnegativity: the
     9	integrand of `consistencyDefect` for two complete measurements placed on
    10	opposite registers is a state quadratic form of a positive operator.  Indeed,
    11	after separating the two placements along the corresponding tensor
    12	bipartition, the off-diagonal sum is
    13	`∑_a (place p₁ E_a) (place p₂ (∑_{b ≠ a} F_b))`, a sum of products of
    14	positive operators supported on complementary registers.  The placement
    15	algebra itself — additivity, the image of zero, positivity and the
    16	commutation of opposite placements — is the shared API of
    17	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Points.PlacementSupport` and
    18	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.LineMeasurement.LinePointOverlap`.
    19	
    20	## References
    21	
    22	The consistency defect is blueprint `def:consistency`, paper
    23	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`.  The
    24	placements and their bipartitions are blueprint `def:expanded-state`, paper
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`.  The
    26	nonnegativity is the hypothesis of items 1 and 2 of
    27	blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1058`.
    29	-/
    30	
    31	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    32	
    33	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    34	
    35	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    36	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    41	
    42	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    43	
    44	/-- Positive operators placed on a directed opposite pair of registers have a
    45	positive product.  Paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`,
    47	blueprint `def:expanded-state`. -/
    48	theorem place_mul_place_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    49	    (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂)
    50	    {X : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₁.side)}
    51	    {Y : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side)}
    52	    (hX : 0 ≤ X) (hY : 0 ≤ Y) :
    53	    0 ≤ S.place p₁ X * S.place p₂ Y := by
    54	  exact Commute.mul_nonneg (S.place_nonneg p₁ hX) (S.place_nonneg p₂ hY)
    55	    (S.place_comm p₁ p₂ hopp X Y)
    56	
    57	end ProjectiveSetting
    58	
    59	/-! ## Nonnegativity of the pointwise consistency defect -/
    60	
    61	/-- The off-diagonal outcome sum of two complete measurements placed on
    62	opposite registers is a positive operator.  Formalization-only auxiliary for
    63	blueprint `def:consistency`, paper
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    65	theorem offDiagonalPlacedProduct_nonneg {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    66	    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    67	    (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂)
    68	    (M₁ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₁.side))
    69	    (M₂ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side)) :
    70	    0 ≤ ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    71	      if a = b then 0
    72	      else S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b) := by
    73	  classical
    74	  have hcomplement : ∀ a : α,
    75	      0 ≤ ∑ b : α, if a = b then (0 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side))
    76	        else M₂.effect b := by
    77	    intro a
    78	    refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => ?_
    79	    by_cases h : a = b
    80	    · rw [if_pos h]

   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test.    413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]

   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
